name: CHROMEWORKS NullGaze Stealth Recon Eye
product_name: Chromeworks NullGaze SR-1 Stealth Recon Ocular
description:
The NullGaze SR-1 is Chromeworks' entry into the restricted surveillance market — a sleek full ocular replacement with a passive-mode exterior indistinguishable from a high-quality cosmetic implant, concealing an 8K continuous-record array with 96-hour onboard encrypted storage. Its low-light amplification provides 6x passive gain in near-darkness with zero active emission, and its facial-recognition countermeasure suite projects a subtle metamaterial scatter field from the sclera surface to defeat third-party FR systems scanning the wearer's face. A secondary iris-pattern randomizer cycles the wearer's biometric signature every 4 hours.

The NullGaze occupies an uncomfortable legal grey zone — sold through Chromeworks' licensed security channels but widely understood to circulate among journalists, spies, corporate investigators, and runners who need eyes that see without being seen. On the Shelf, the SR-1's ability to defeat facial recognition makes it a survival tool for anyone who needs to move through CorpSec-monitored transit corridors without a logged identity trail.
installation_requirements: Standard ocular socket surgery; Chromeworks-certified installer required; restricted purchase license needed for facial-recognition countermeasure activation
rejection_risk: Low — Chromeworks premium biocompatible housing; neural integration smooth but record-mode activation can cause brief visual static during first month
maintenance: Monthly encrypted storage offload recommended; quarterly scatter-field emitter cleaning; annual iris-randomizer recalibration

cultural_context: The NullGaze has become the implicit standard equipment of GLMZ's investigative journalism underground and corporate espionage circuit alike — a tool that erases the face wearing it while capturing everything it sees. CorpSec divisions maintain a dedicated detection protocol specifically for the SR-1's scatter-field signature.

story_hooks: A NullGaze unit's 96-hour archive washed up in a storm drain — still encrypted, still intact, and its previous owner is missing
